hints.title: Distance Bounded Duplicate Obstacle
hints.text: Checking all pairs of elements takes quadratic time. How can you maintain only the elements within the recent window of distance at most k?

hints.title: Window Set Invariant
hints.text: Maintain a set of elements seen in the current window of size at most k. If the current number already exists in the set, a valid nearby duplicate is found.

hints.title: Sliding Window Set Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty set seen. For each index i and number val: if val in seen, return True. Add val to seen. If len(seen) > k, remove nums[i - k] from seen. If the loop completes, return False.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Sliding window set of maximum size min(N, k) offering O(1) average lookup and eviction.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing all pairs within distance k takes O(N * k) time which reaches 10^10 operations for large k.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Set auxiliary memory bounded by min(N, k) achieves linear runtime.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Managing the sliding window set eviction logic cleanly when index exceeds k.
